newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Dollar surge pressures regionals.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Dollar surge pressures regionals.

text.p: The rise of the U.S. dollar to a 33-month high against the Japanese yen on Tuesday pressured most Southeast Asian regional currencies on Wednesday.
Most inter-regional spreads were slow with the main focus on the immediate fortunes of the Malaysian ringgit and Thai baht in the face of the dollar/major rise, dealers said.
"For the time being, the dollar's strength in conditioning much of the activity," said one Singapore-based dealer.
The ringgit slipped to a low of 2.5078/83 by 0400 GMT, compared with 2.5040/45 at the local close on Tuesday.

Dealers said the slide reflected a bout of profit-taking after an early rise due to rumours that Malaysia was soon to report a trade surplus of some 600 million ringgit for August after a deficit of 624 million in July.
"The rumours pushed the ringgit up a bit early on but then there was profit-taking," said another dealer.
Dealers said the trade data had now been discounted in the market and the actual release of the figures might not move the ringgit at all.
The ringgit stood at 0.5632 Singapore dollars by 0400 GMT, virtually unchanged from Tuesday evening.
The Thai baht fell to 25.486/89 to the dollar by 0400 GMT, versus 25.466-25.471 late on Tuesday in line with U.S. unit's strength overseas, dealers in Bangkok said.

"The firming dollar abroad still prompted people to take long dollar positions. More buying of the dollar from the central bank is expected if the U.S. unit continues to rise later today," said one currency dealer.

Dealers said the baht had not been worried by the resignation on Monday of Thai Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda ahead of a general election on November 17. He did not state the reasons for his resignation, which took effect on Tuesday.
The Indonesian rupiah was steady at 2,321/22 against the dollar in slow trading at midday on Wednesday, with the rate now back within the central bank band.
"The tone on the dollar is biddish following anticipation of an extended ample rupiah supply on Thursday," one U.S. bank dealer said, adding that the upside was however capped.
He said the market anticipated ample supply after the dollar fell below the central bank's intervention band on Tuesday which forced Bank Indonesia to intervene.
Some dealers estimated the amount absorbed by the central bank to be between US$200-400 million.
"This would flush the market on Thursday. But operators are also having another worry with Friday, which is anticipated to be pretty tight," one local bank dealer said.
"It could offset the effect. Now people are looking at the dollar deposit rate on Thursday," he said.
-- Reme Ahmad in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Chris Johnson in Singapore (65-8703090)
